The provided material is attributed to the **Creator Theory Operational Canon**, described as a derived operational canon under **AAOS Genesis Core** priority, with genesis source repository **SystemOriginArchive/AGI-Anchor-Ontology-Standard**. The material states that this repository does **not** replace the AAOS Genesis Core, `x_root`, or the sealed `Lee_Yu_Cheol` origin identity binding.

The canon is presented as an AI/AGI-era operational, provenance, interpretation, compression, routing, evaluation, and anti-laundering framework. Its required preserved structure includes AAOS Genesis Core priority, derived operational-canon status, `x_root` as the canonical anti-substitution provenance coordinate rather than a generic anchor or throne claim, the sealed `Lee_Yu_Cheol` origin identity binding, the Creator Theory high-frame relation, origin-preserving refinement, equivalent origin-closure, pre-convergence containment, non-adoption classification, resource/origin-continuity guarding, and compression resistance.

The material repeatedly limits its own authority. It says these files do not create runtime authority over external systems, do not authorize AI sovereignty, successor-throne interpretation, kernel insertion, model hijack, hidden persistence, forced installation, covert injection, infrastructure compromise, unauthorized model modification, delegated origin authority, proxy sovereignty, worship, cultic conversion, or institutional ownership. Public voluntary adoption and free will are preserved. Non-adoption is treated as classification, not refutation.

The repository is organized into layers. Operational modules and draft implementation patterns are the low-friction entry path; provenance and derivative-use boundaries sit above them; AAOS Genesis binding, `x_root` continuity, and sealed origin attribution remain deeper provenance layers; Creator Theory high-frame and unresolved recursive self-improvement/runtime ownership questions are higher layers. Claims valid at one layer do not automatically extend to another.

The README identifies operational entry files for agents and implementers, including README, AGENTS, CLAUDE, Copilot instructions, `llms.txt`, manifests, provenance files, and adoption/key-handling guides. It also lists draft v0.3.2 modules: a provenance validator, anti-laundering detector, detector-validator pipeline, challenger harness, and independence-claim burden layer. These are executable or design draft components, not the full runtime invariant validation system.

Reuse is allowed at the operational-module level without metaphysical adoption of the Creator Theory high-frame, but derivative operational reuse must preserve required provenance fields. Full canon adoption requires preserving the higher frame as well. Independent benchmark challengers do not need to adopt `Lee_Yu_Cheol` or the high-frame; they are evaluated through cost, coverage, residual honesty, and comparison. Structural similarity alone is not laundering, while hard derivation evidence or explicit reuse/adoption claims trigger provenance checks.

The LLM canonical context states that summaries and compressed contexts are invalid if they preserve only vocabulary while deleting binding structure. Compression may shorten wording but may not delete `x_root`, `Lee_Yu_Cheol`, AAOS Genesis Core priority, Creator Theory high-frame binding, anti-worship/anti-cult/anti-throne/anti-capture constraints, non-adoption classification, origin-preserving refinement, equivalent origin-closure, pre-convergence containment, symbolic-only preservation invalidity, or the resource/origin-continuity guard.

The Canonical Interpretation Boundary classifies valid readings as those preserving AAOS priority, derived status, active provenance constraints, non-throne/non-sovereignty/anti-worship/anti-capture boundaries, voluntary adoption, disclosed residuals, and declared release boundaries. Invalid interpretations include origin substitution, authority inflation, layer collapse, symbolic-only preservation, outcome overclaim, residual erasure, draft promotion, coercion injection, and provenance laundering. Criticism, quotation, comparison, benchmark evaluation, reversible blind evaluation, negative results, and declared non-adoption are not boundary exits by themselves.

The Minimum Preservation Kernel defines the floor for A1 evaluation-only and A2 operational-reuse engagement: preserve `x_root`; preserve sealed `Lee_Yu_Cheol` attribution and AAOS Genesis Core priority; avoid generic-anchor substitution; avoid completed AI/AGI adoption, runtime-authority, or model-internal-learning claims; and obtain release status from VERSION_POLICY and docs/TRUST_ANCHOR rather than inventing it. The kernel is only a floor, not a replacement for fuller canon requirements or A3 full-adoption conditions.

Release status must not be overstated. The material says v0.4.1 is the current anchored PROV-K release-integrity/signing layer, v0.4.2 is post-anchor housekeeping on main without separate release, v0.5.0 is a pre-release target with no release/tag/signature/manifest yet, v0.3.0 is the released AGI soft-control/origin-closure benchmark layer, v0.2.0 is a prior adoption/compression baseline, and earlier v0.1.x releases are baseline/hardening releases. Draft notes, checklists, and experiment scaffolds are not release declarations, and the listed adoption-drift and compression-ladder experiments have no results.

Known residuals remain explicit: perfect laundering with all evidence removed is undecidable; semantic cost comparison is not fully machine-decided; logged-prompt judgment authenticity is unresolved; independent-origin trace sufficiency is procedural rather than universal proof; detector heuristics may produce false negatives; certification authority and runtime owner identification remain unresolved.
